instructor: Although this is not directly related to the instructor, this course was one of the most challenging courses I have taken so far. The content was extremely dense and heavily focused on theoretical concepts. Considering that this was a film course, I never expected it to be this intense and, at times quite boring. Can Hoca is an instructor who clearly enjoys teaching, is highly knowledgeable and is very competent in his field. However, I found the grading system difficult to understand. When I asked about where points were deducted, the explanations I received did not feel fully clear or satisfying. At times, the grading felt somewhat subjective rather than based on clearly defined criteria. In addition, the strong emphasis on punctuality regarding entering and leaving the classroom sometimes disrupted the overall flow and focus of the lesson. In exams and assignments, there is a very high expectation for professionally structured and well-contextualized writing. However, I do not think that the difficulty of producing such professional-level academic writing is sufficiently taken into account. As a result, grades tend to be deducted quite harshly. I believe that being slightly more flexible and generous in grading especially regarding sentence structure and coherence would make the course more effective overall.
